FAQ_CATS.label: About the platform and the firm
qs: Is UAE Expat Wills a government website?

No. UAE Expat Wills is an independent digital legal-service platform owned and operated by Summit Legal Consultancy UAE, Trade Licence No. 4429232.01. It is not a court, government authority, notary or official Will registry.
Who actually prepares my Will?
Summit Legal Consultancy UAE. The platform delivers the digital process — assessment, questionnaire, document exchange and status — while the legal services and human review are provided by the firm.
Who will I be dealing with?
Summit's legal team, led by Ahmed Mohammedi, Managing Director and Co-Founder, and Dr. Mohamed Raouf, Principal Legal Consultant and Co-Founder.
Is this a template or document-generator service?
No. A draft is prepared for your circumstances and every Will receives human legal review before it is treated as ready for your approval. No automated draft is released to a client.
Do you give legal advice through the website content?
No. The information on the website is general. Advice is given within an accepted engagement, after the legal team has reviewed your instructions.
Does using the website create a professional engagement?

No. Visiting the site, completing the assessment, creating an account, sending an enquiry or uploading documents does not by itself create a professional engagement. An engagement begins when Summit accepts the matter and the applicable terms are agreed.
Can Summit decline my matter?

Yes. Summit may decline where a matter falls outside our services, creates a conflict, lacks sufficient information, cannot be handled appropriately through the platform, or cannot lawfully or professionally be accepted.
Is my Will registered because I completed the questionnaire or paid?

No. Completing the assessment, paying the professional fee, completing the questionnaire or approving a draft does not itself register a Will. Registration or notarisation is completed only through the competent authority.
Where is Summit based?
Summit Legal Consultancy UAE is licensed in the United Arab Emirates under Trade Licence No. 4429232.01. Contact is by email and WhatsApp; no address is published on this site.

FAQ_CATS.label: Fees and payment
qs: How much does a standard UAE Will cost?
The professional fee for one accepted standard Will is AED {fee} plus VAT.
What does that fee include?

Will preparation, human legal review by Summit's legal team, certified legal translation of the new UAE Will, the amendment allowance stated in your Service Confirmation, and assistance submitting the application to the competent authority.
Are government and court fees included?

No. Government, court, registry, notary, certification, attestation, courier and identity-verification charges are separate unless expressly included in writing. They are set and collected by the relevant authority or provider.
What are the current authority charges?

As currently published: ADJD Civil Will AED 950.00 for one regular Will; Dubai Courts approximately AED 2,100.00 for one Will; DIFC varies by Will type. Each remains subject to the authority's current schedule and to the route confirmed after legal review.
How much is a DIFC Will?
DIFC engagements are quoted individually and currently start from AED 3,999 plus VAT. A DIFC matter is never shown as a fixed purchasable price and cannot be paid for online.
Do a couple pay twice?

Each person's Will is a separate document and a separate authority registration. The total professional fee and any package treatment is shown in the Service Confirmation before payment. Authority fees normally apply separately to each Will.
When do I pay?

After the assessment, once you have created an account and read the engagement terms. You see the proposed service, the fee and VAT, what is included, the amendment allowance, known exclusions and the separate charge categories before you commit.
Could I be charged more later?

Only with your express approval. If the detailed information reveals work outside the accepted scope, Summit pauses the affected work, explains what has changed and provides the proposed scope and fee. You may accept or decline.
What happens if legal review says I need a DIFC Will after I have paid?

The matter is paused and the full standard fee already paid is credited against the agreed DIFC professional fee. If you decline, the unused balance is refunded after deducting only a reasonable, documented amount for substantive work already completed.
Am I asked to pay while my case is under review?
No. No payment is requested while a matter is held for legal review.

FAQ_CATS.label: Eligibility and routes
qs: Can Muslims use UAE Expat Wills?

Yes. Muslim clients complete the same online process as everyone else: provide instructions, pay the professional fee, and Summit's legal team reviews the case, confirms the correct wording under the applicable rules and selects the appropriate registration authority before you approve anything.
Can UAE citizens use the service?
The Will services available through this platform are not intended for UAE citizens. You are welcome to contact Summit Legal Consultancy UAE for other legal services.
Do I need to be a UAE resident?

Not necessarily. A non-resident who owns UAE assets may still need a UAE Will. Residency affects the route analysis but does not by itself decide it, and each authority applies its own current requirements.
Do I have to choose the registration route myself?
No. You do not choose between the pathways. Both begin with the same assessment, and the appropriate route is identified by the legal review.
Which routes exist?

A possible route may involve the DIFC Courts Wills Service, Abu Dhabi Judicial Department Civil Wills, Dubai Courts or another legally appropriate process. The comparison on the UAE Will Options page sets out who each may be relevant for.

FAQ_CATS.label: The process and timing
qs: How long does the assessment take?
About five minutes. It is free and no account is needed.
How many questions are there?
It depends on your answers — conditional questions appear only when they are relevant, so we do not promise a number.
How quickly will I get my first draft?

For an accepted standard matter we aim to send the first draft within 2 business days after receiving complete, usable instructions and all required documents. A matter requiring specialist analysis, further clarification or additional documents may take longer.
How long does registration take?
That is set by the competent authority. We cannot guarantee that any authority will accept a Will or complete registration within a particular period.
Can I save and come back?
Yes. Assessment answers are kept against your device until you create an account, and questionnaire progress is saved to your account after that.
What if my circumstances change during the process?

Tell us. Before registration, a material change such as marriage, divorce, separation, birth or adoption, the death or incapacity of a chosen person, or the acquisition or disposal of a significant asset may affect the draft.
What does 'held for legal review' mean?

It means one or more answers indicate that the legal team should look at your matter before recommending a service, a route or a price. It is not a rejection, and no payment is requested while a matter is held.

FAQ_CATS.label: Guardianship and family
qs: Can I name a guardian for my children?
You can record guardianship wishes where the selected Will route permits it. A nomination records your wishes; it does not remove the rights of the other parent, and the competent court decides.
Will the court appoint the person I name?
We cannot promise that. The competent court decides guardianship, taking the applicable law and the child's interests into account.
What if my first choice cannot act?
You can name alternatives — for beneficiaries, executors and guardians — in case a first choice dies, declines or is unable to act.
Do I need to name my children individually?
The detailed questionnaire asks for the information needed for the accepted scope. No names are required during the free assessment.
Can I provide for an unmarried partner or a stepchild?
Naming them is the only way the intention is recorded, and some routes limit who may benefit. The legal review confirms what is possible on your route.

FAQ_CATS.label: Registration and the authorities
qs: Who registers the Will?
The competent authority, not the platform and not Summit. We assist with preparation and submission and explain the authority's requirements.
Will the authority definitely accept my Will?
No one can promise that. The authority may set its own eligibility, document, language, identity, attendance and signing requirements, and it decides whether to accept a Will for registration.
Do I have to attend in person?
That depends on the route and the authority's current rules. Some routes currently permit virtual registration; others require attendance. We tell you what applies before submission.
Is the authority fee paid to Summit?
No. It is set and collected by the authority. After legal review confirms the recommended route, we explain the then-current charge before you authorise or make that payment.
Does registration mean the Will cannot be challenged?
No. Registration is an authority process. It does not guarantee future validity, enforcement or any particular outcome after death.
Does a registered Will avoid probate?
Not automatically. The chosen framework can affect the court dealing with probate or implementation, document language, enforcement steps and asset-transfer procedures.
Will my UAE Will work in my home country?
One document does not operate automatically in every country. Where a foreign Will exists, the review considers how the two documents sit together.
Is the Will translated?
Certified legal translation of the new UAE Will is included in the standard professional fee. Legalisation, recognition or translation of a separate foreign document is not.

FAQ_CATS.label: Documents, privacy and security
qs: What documents will I need?

Typically your passport and Emirates ID, plus any document relevant to the accepted scope — an existing Will, a title deed, a shareholders' agreement. We ask for what the route requires and nothing more.
Can I photograph documents on my phone?
Yes. Upload supports camera capture on mobile.
How is my information handled?

In accordance with the Privacy Policy. Will instructions may contain sensitive personal information about you and other people, so please do not upload information that is not reasonably required for your matter.
Should I email sensitive details?
No. Email and messaging carry confidentiality and delivery risks. Once a matter is accepted, documents are exchanged through your secure account.
Will you ever ask for my password or card details by message?
Never. We do not request passwords, seed phrases, private keys or card details by email, WhatsApp or telephone.
Who at Summit can see my answers?
Access is limited to the staff who need it to deliver your matter. Certain sensitive answers are restricted to authorised legal staff and are excluded from ordinary notifications and case lists.

FAQ_CATS.label: Changes, amendments and after registration
qs: Can I change my Will after it is drafted?
Yes, within the amendment allowance stated in your Service Confirmation. Further amendments may be chargeable, and any charge is explained and approved before it applies.
Can I change it after registration?
A registered Will can normally be replaced or revoked, subject to the authority's process. Contact us and we will explain the route for an update.
What if I approve a draft and later find an error?

Tell us. If you approved a document containing an error you could reasonably have identified, or a relevant fact was not disclosed, correction work may be chargeable. This does not affect your rights where the error was ours.
What if I want to revoke an existing Will?
Say so in the assessment. A matter involving revoking or replacing an existing Will is reviewed by the legal team before payment.
Do you remind me to review my Will?
We provide a route for future updates when your family, assets or wishes change. A Will should be reviewed after any significant life event.
Can I get my documents after the matter closes?
Yes. Final documents are available in your account, and you can ask us for copies.
How do I make a complaint?

Email info@uaeexpatwills.com with your name, matter reference, the issue and the outcome you are requesting. Using our internal process does not prevent you from contacting a competent UAE consumer-protection, data-protection, regulatory or judicial authority.

PROFILES.title: A parent of minor children
PROFILES.body: Guardianship is the decision most people are actually here for. Where the selected Will route permits it, you can record who you would want to care for your children and who should act if that person cannot.
PROFILES.consider: A nomination records your wishes. It does not remove the rights of the other parent, and the competent court decides.

PROFILES.title: Part of a blended family or a previous marriage
PROFILES.body: Children from different relationships, a former spouse, and a current partner can produce an outcome nobody intended. A Will states who receives what, in your own words.
PROFILES.consider: Bring any existing Will and any family, matrimonial or separation agreement to the review.

PROFILES.title: A UAE property owner, account holder or investor
PROFILES.body: Property, bank accounts, brokerage accounts and end-of-service entitlements may each be treated differently depending on the route and the authority.
PROFILES.consider: Asset type and location affect which framework is appropriate.

PROFILES.title: Supporting an unmarried partner, stepchild, relative or charity
PROFILES.body: A person or organisation you support informally may have no automatic entitlement. Naming them is the only way the intention is recorded.
PROFILES.consider: Some routes limit who may benefit; the review confirms what is possible.

PROFILES.title: A business owner or shareholder
PROFILES.body: A shareholding may be governed by a shareholders' agreement or the company's own constitution as well as by your Will.
PROFILES.consider: The two documents are read together, which is why the review asks for both.

PROFILES.title: Holding assets or an existing Will in more than one country
PROFILES.body: One document does not operate automatically in every country. A UAE Will can sit alongside a foreign Will, but the two need to be coordinated rather than assumed to agree.
PROFILES.consider: Where a foreign Will exists, the review considers whether anything needs revoking or amending.

PROFILES.title: A married couple preparing coordinated but separate Wills
PROFILES.body: A couple does not share one Will. Each person gives their own instructions and personally approves their own document, even when the two are prepared together.
PROFILES.consider: Each Will is a separate document and a separate authority registration.

PROFILES.title: A non-resident who owns UAE assets
PROFILES.body: You do not need a UAE residence visa to hold UAE assets, and you do not necessarily need one to use every route. What applies depends on the authority's current requirements.
PROFILES.consider: Residency affects the route analysis but does not by itself decide it.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what personal information UAE Expat Wills collects, why, how it is handled and what rights you have. Will instructions may contain sensitive information about you and about other people, so the platform collects only what a matter reasonably requires.
clauses: Who controls your information
Summit Legal Consultancy UAE, Trade Licence No. 4429232.01, is responsible for personal information processed through the platform.
What we collect
Assessment answers, account and identity details, matter information and documents, payment records, communications, and technical information such as device and log data.
Why we collect it
To assess your enquiry, deliver an accepted service, meet legal and professional obligations, secure the platform and communicate with you about your matter.
Sensitive answers

Certain answers — including any answer indicating a capacity or influence concern — are restricted to authorised legal staff, are excluded from ordinary notifications and case lists, and are not used for marketing.
Declining to answer
Where a question offers it, you may decline to answer. Declining may mean a matter is reviewed manually rather than continuing through the standard online pathway.
Who we share it with
Service providers who help deliver the service under contract, the competent authority where submission requires it, and others where the law requires. We do not sell personal information.
Retention
We keep matter records for as long as necessary for the service, and afterwards for the periods required by law and professional obligation.
Your rights
You may ask for access to your information, correction of inaccurate information, or deletion where the law permits. Contact info@uaeexpatwills.com.
Security
Access is limited to staff who need it. Documents are exchanged through your secure account rather than by email once a matter is accepted.

After the assessment and after you have read the engagement terms. No payment is requested while a matter is held for legal review.
What the fee covers
The professional work stated in your Service Confirmation for one accepted standard Will: AED {fee} plus VAT.
What is charged separately
Government, court, registry, notary, certification, attestation, courier and identity-verification charges, and any work outside the accepted scope that you have approved.
Cancelling before work begins

The matter is paused and the standard fee already paid is credited against the agreed DIFC professional fee. If you decline the DIFC quotation, the unused balance is refunded on the same basis.

Where Summit declines a matter after payment, the professional fee is refunded, less only a reasonable, documented amount for substantive work already completed.

An authority charge already paid to an authority is outside our control and is subject to that authority's own rules.

To the original payment method where possible, within a reasonable period after the refund is agreed.

Small files stored on your device that let a site remember your session, your preferences and your progress.
Strictly necessary cookies
Required to run the platform: your session, security, and your saved assessment progress. These cannot be switched off.
Preference cookies

Analytics cookies

Changes to this policy

Contact

COOKIE_CATS.label: Strictly necessary
COOKIE_CATS.body: Your session, security, and the assessment answers held against this device. Without these the platform cannot run, so they cannot be switched off.

COOKIE_CATS.label: Preferences
COOKIE_CATS.body: Remembers this cookie choice, and your language if you set one, so you are not asked again on every page.

COOKIE_CATS.label: Analytics
COOKIE_CATS.body: Counts which pages are used and where people stop, so the assessment can be improved. Aggregated, and never linked to your answers.

COOKIE_CATS.label: Marketing
COOKIE_CATS.body: Measures whether a campaign brought you here. Off by default and not required to use the service.

404.title: That page is not here
404.body: The address you followed does not match a page on this site. A link may have been mistyped, or a page may have been renamed.
404.detail: Nothing has gone wrong with your matter. If you were partway through the assessment, your answers are still held against this device and you can pick them up where you left off.
404.aside: The assessment, the pricing page, or the FAQs. All three are linked from the footer of every page.

500.title: Something on our side failed
500.body: The page could not be built because of a fault on our servers, not anything you did. The fault has been logged and our team has been notified automatically.
500.detail: If you were partway through a form, your last saved step is intact. Nothing has been submitted twice and no payment has been taken as a result of this.
500.aside: Email us with the reference below and roughly what you were doing. It lets us find the exact fault in the log rather than guessing.

expired.title: That link has expired
expired.body: Links to your questionnaire and your documents are time-limited, which is what stops a forwarded email from opening your matter. This one has passed its window.
expired.detail: Your matter is unaffected and nothing has been lost. Sign in and the same page will be waiting, or ask us to send a new link.
expired.aside: A questionnaire link lasts 24 hours. A password reset link lasts one hour. Both can be used once.

revoked.title: This session was signed out
revoked.body: You were signed out because a new password was set on your account, or because you or our team revoked this device. It was not an error.
revoked.detail: If you did not expect this, contact us before signing in again — we will check the access record on your account with you.
revoked.aside: Setting a new password signs out every other device. A session also ends after 30 minutes without activity, or when you sign out.
